advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test driving `_paged_search` against a client returning (a) repeated keyless (key=None) pages — asserting it does NOT raise BackendPaginationStallError and terminates, and (b) a repeated non-dict head — asserting no AttributeError escapes the guard.
evidence: _base.py:180-185: `# A missing/unusable key yields None, which never compares equal to a previous None here — two consecutive keyless pages must not be read as a stall, and a non-dict item ... must not raise an AttributeError from the guard itself.`
_base.py:186: `if first_key is not None and first_key == prev_first_key:`

ABSENCE: search of test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py for `non-dict` / `without a key` / `isinstance(head, dict)` returned no matches; the added `_OffsetBlindClient` always serves pages whose head is a dict carrying `key=f"DC-{i}"`, so neither the None-key nor the non-dict-head path is ever executed.
advisory.finding: The new keyless-page / non-dict-head defensive branch added to `_paged_search` is untested. The guard `first_key = head.get("key") if isinstance(head, dict) else None` plus the `if first_key is not None and first_key == prev_first_key` check encodes two contracts stated in the code comment — two consecutive keyless (key=None) pages must NOT be read as a stall, and a non-dict head must NOT raise AttributeError — but no test in the added suite drives a client that returns repeated keyless or non-dict-head pages. A regression that dropped the `first_key is not None` guard (turning two None-keyed pages into a false stall) or the `isinstance(head, dict)` guard (turning a non-dict head into an AttributeError) would pass all added tests.
